title: The life of a task: ticket, branch, pull request, review, merge, release

videos.script: Somebody notices a problem. The bakery closes on public holidays, and the site does not say so. Two customers have already turned up to a locked door. {{problem}} Between that moment and the day the site says it, a lot happens, and most of it is not typing. {{between}} The problem is written down as a ticket, with a number. Somebody picks it up. They start a branch from the newest main, and they name it after the ticket. {{ticket}} They make a few small commits, push them, and open a pull request. Somebody else reads it, asks for a change, and approves. {{pr}} It is merged. The ticket closes. And some time later a release goes out, and the notice is finally in front of the people who needed it. {{release}} You already know every Git command in this story. What this lesson adds is the order they come in, and the thread that ties them together. That thread is the ticket's number, which turns up in the branch, in the commits, in the pull request and in the release. {{thread}} Six months from now somebody will ask why this line is here. That number is how they will find out. {{why}} By the end, you will be able to take a task from a ticket to production, and answer the question every team eventually asks: is it live yet? {{title}}
